articles.title: The pest I’ll never forget: the cockerel whose crowing almost destroyed me
articles.description: When a neighbour installed a braying bird on the roof of our block of flats, the noise was relentless from sunrise till sunset. It became the sinister soundtrack to my life You can’t choose your family or your colleagues. And you definitely can’t choose your neighbours: the people with whom you involuntarily share a postcode and the ritual of swapping misdelivered Amazon parcels. For the most part, the neighbours in my block of flats are reassuringly neighbourly. During lockdown, I became unofficial IT support for one trying to home-school her son. I spent years emailing a PR man about Guardian celebrity interviews without realising he lived two doors away. And one of my neighbours (and now my hero) used to be in the 80s punk band Splodgenessabounds, who sang Two Pints of Lager and a Packet of Crisps Please. The other half I couldn’t pick out of a police lineup, although I certainly know their habits, from the phantom non-recycler who bungs all their plastic bottles and newspapers in the normal black bin, to the mystery resident who happily leaves the security gate open. But the one that is lodged most firmly in my memory is the neighbour who, last year, kept a pet cockerel on the roof. At least, I assume it was a pet. I can’t think of any other reason that doesn’t sound considerably more sinister. Continue reading...
